This is the nature of our enemy.'='我在毕业典礼上因我的坚韧、胆量和缺乏想象力而受到赞扬。我发现自己最近越来越多地回归到这些美德。我已下令将望远镜完全对准天蓝色。我们感受到了它的全部威力。我看到了阴影，精神，幻觉。有时，我觉得我被玩弄了。就在前天晚上，我被一束蓝色的星光惊醒，就在望远镜上方。我蹑手蹑脚地走到那里，独自站在夜的边缘。我感到被审判了。我的一切可以被煮成原子，散落到地平线最远的边缘，而它仍然会追寻我，直到连风都不敢嚎叫我的名字。而一旦我变成最小的尘埃分子，它就会完全忘记我，它的注意力固定在一些更伟大的设计上。这就是我们敌人的本性。
'Incandescent fire on the horizon. A warning? A welcome? Sometimes I think they speak in sigils to confound us. Dolton has proved useless, as ever. Perhaps I shall make a pyre of his books and use the ashes to draw the Correspondence in my notes. Your boots are soon stained red-gold. \r\n\r\nYou push through the shrouded gloom until you come upon a grove, deep in the undergrowth. Great stems bend to form arches like cathedral vaults. A canopy of petals, gold and cerise, forms its roof. \r\n\r\nWithin the grove, a single flower grows, stunted and pale. It is a miniature of those that tower above it. Its petals are soft and fragile as spun sugar. Its stem is covered in mould. Yet, in its shape, and the sad echo of its colours, this little flower is the mirror of all of those that now tower above it. Perhaps it was the first, before its offspring outgrew it.\r\n\r\nYou do not linger. He is fascinated by their red faces, their bristling moustaches, their pointing fingers and clenched fists.\r\n\r\nThe Eccentric joins you. "Beleth admires force," she whispers.\r\n\r\nHe would fit in at the Floating Parliament, where MPs push their beliefs into law using words as swords and procedure as nooses.\r\n\r\n"Yes," the Eccentric muses. "I think he'd like that. And I know what he'd find intolerable: dreams. Those dreams where the rules all change and your strength is useless. The roses of Caduceus could help."=布锐斯在走廊从你身边冲撞而过。他听到两个司炉在争吵。当他发现他们时，他全神贯注地看着，带着古代哲人王的气质。他被他们的红脸、他们的小胡子、他们的手指和紧握的拳头所吸引。\n\n猫咪怪人来到了你身边。“布锐斯崇拜武力，”她低声说。\n\n他很适合浮空议院，在那里，议员们化语言为刀剑，化程序为绞索，化信念为法令。\n\n“不错，”猫咪怪人思忖道，“我想他会喜欢这样。而且我知道他受不了什么东西：梦。使规则改变，力量无用的梦。商神宫的玫瑰可以帮助你。”

Beleth has departed.=Beleth已经离开了。

Beyond the antique facades of the Lane of Lions and Unicorns, the Empyrean rises high in steel and blue light. The constraints of its location necessitate that the Empyrean builds upwards.\r\n\r\nCareful porticoes give way to expansive temples and crowded markets. People live cheek by jowl. Light is precious, and easily lost. Power is conserved carefully; when times are bad whole districts go dark. It would be easy for hopelessness to seep in; the Khan occupies his people with festivals, celebrating his people's history of the old Khanate, and constant technological innovation. December is... well, you don't know what December is. But they are older and vaster than you, and they hate the stars.=十二月是……嗯，你不知道十二月是什么。但它比你更古老，更宏大，而且它讨厌星星。
December spoke to you like a comrade; like a friend.=十二月对你说话，就像一个同志；像一个朋友。
December spoke to you like a comrade; like a friend. They shared a doubt that preyed upon them, and you dissected it like doctors.\r\n\r\nIt is difficult to recall more details of your conversation. December spoke about the edifice of the universe, and the parts in its machine. Of a great Chain that binds us all in our place. It all made sense at the time, fitting together like the cogs in a clock. Now, you would struggle to tell it to others. It is as if you were both speaking in another language, which has now fallen from your mind.=十二月像一位同志、一位朋友一样和你说话。它分享着困扰它的疑虑，而你像医生一样剖析它。\\n\\n很难回忆起你们谈话的更多细节。十二月谈及宇宙的广厦，以及其机关的部件。一个大锁链将我们所有的人捆绑在我们的位置上。这一切在当时都是有意义的，就像时钟中的齿轮一样啮合。现在，你很难向别人讲述这件事。仿佛你们之前在用另一种语言说话，而这种语言现在已经从你的头脑中消失了。
December steeples an unlikely number of elegant fingers, and speaks of a time when cordiality between the stars failed; when constellations and conjunctions went to war.=十二月竖起一个不太可能的优雅的手指，说到了一个星星之间的友好关系失败的时候；当星座和结点开战的时候。
December steeples an unlikely number of elegant fingers, and speaks of a time when cordiality between the stars failed; when constellations and conjunctions went to war.\r\n\r\nThe Courtesy was the agreement that ended it. The stars agreed a set of permissions and ceremonies that must precede any murder of a star. Now, the sky is littered with dead suns, but all agree that the murders were committed with a due sense of decorum.\r\n\r\nThere December stops. There is more, they say, but to speak it would hasten a battle December is not yet willing to fight. You stumble from Corncrake house, your memory of the conversation already beginning to flake. You had better talk to the Masked Citizen before it collapses entirely.=十二月交叠起许多根修长手指，语及那个群星剑拔弩张的年代：星座与合相反目成仇，烽烟遍布天野。\n\n仪节终结了那场战争。群星约定，唯有事先遵循既定的许可与礼仪，方可行使对一颗星辰的杀戮。如今，天野中遍布殒日，但群星都默认，杀戮皆合乎体统。\n\n至此，十二月停下了话语，表示有更多真相尚待揭露，但倘若言之过早，将催生一场自己无意参与的战争。你踉跄着走出长脚秧鸡之家，方才的对话已开始淡忘。你最好在彻底遗忘之前尽快去找蒙面公民。

Half an hour into your explorations, the wind picks up.=在你探索的半个小时后，风起了。
Half an hour into your explorations, the wind picks up. The caves fill with the sound of distant fluting. There is no tune to it, just a pleasant, natural melody, like the echo of birdsong. Just as quickly though, it turns sharp. Less birdsong, more bird prey to a ravenous cat. The atonal screech rocks the mountain, though by the time it leaves the caves, their unique acoustics have turned it too into something soft.\r\n\r\nYour feet crunch against something. A shard of glass, red-tinted. Looking through one side, the world seems a burning inferno. From the other, all is well. Looking closer, part of a glyph remains on the shard. Extremely precise work, though its function is alien to you. Perhaps there is someone in Lustrum who would know more.=你探索了半个小时后，风大了起来。山洞里充满了渺远的笛声。它没有曲调，只有一种悦耳、自然的旋律，像是鸟鸣的回响。但很快，它就变得尖锐起来。不再像是鸟鸣，更像是鸟被饥饿的猫猎食。这无声调的尖啸震动着整座山，但当它离开洞穴时，也被其独特的传音效果变得柔和。\n\n你的脚碰到了什么。一块玻璃碎片，带着淡淡的红光。透过它的一面看去，世界就像是一个燃烧的地狱。从另一面看去，一切安好。仔细观察，能发现碎片上留有一个符号的一部分。作工极其精湛，但它的机理对你而言是陌生的。也许伍载镇会有人知道更多。

Ignoring the Minister's protests, you haul the Vagabond to safety. The well-winds die as quickly as they had risen.\r\n\r\n"Why?" shouts the Minister, into the darkness below. "Why give him another reprieve?"\r\n\r\nAs you haul the Vagabond back to your engine, his broken fingers lengthen; his legs collapse in a tangle of pallid tendrils. He writhes, briefly, until his limbs petrify.\r\n\r\nBy the time you reach the engine, his right arm is a creaking branch. Below the waist, he is a trunk of white wood, ending in a snarl of twitching roots. Your crew stare in revulsion.\r\n\r\nAt your urging, they carry him to his quarters and stand him up on his roots. You can only see the whites of his eyes; small, keening noises escape between his lips. He claws at the bark of his branch-arm as though hoping to find flesh beneath.\r\n\r\nYou back away, giving the Dendrified Vagabond a moment to recover. After that? He can still perform his duties aboard the engine, you suspect. And who else would take him in?=无视传教士的抗议，你将流浪汉拉回安全地带。井风瞬间消失，如同它们涌现时一样迅速。\\n\\n“为什么？”传教士朝着黑暗深渊喊道，“为什么还要给他缓刑？”\\n\\n当你将流浪汉带回机车时，他断裂的手指渐渐延伸；他的双腿在苍白肢体纠缠中崩溃。他短暂地挣扎着，直到四肢僵化。\\n\\n等到你抵达机车时，他的右臂已经变成了一根咯吱作响的树枝。腰部以下，他是一截苍白的木头，尖端是一丛颤动的树根。你的列车员惊恐地盯着这个景象。\\n\\n在你的催促下，他们将流浪汉抬到他的住处，并让他以自己的根为支撑站立。此刻你只能看到他眼中泛着白光；微弱而哀伤的声音从唇间逸出。他用爪子挠着自己那如树枝般硬化了的手臂，仿佛试图从中找到肉体。\\n\\n你后退一步，给木质化的流浪汉一个喘息的机会。之后呢？你怀疑他仍然可以在机车上执行任务。而且，还有谁会收留他呢？

Langley Hall is a labyrinth of well intentioned jollity. Parties snake from the front door to the back kitchen by way of a thousand bedrooms, bathrooms, billiard rooms and ballrooms. The wine flows like water, and the hour is always hazily too late. Those that come here rarely leave, and those that do rarely do so for long. They have made a home of Langley Hall, or at least, Langley Hall has made for them a home.=兰利厅是一个欢乐的迷宫，其中满溢着善意。派对从前门蜿蜒到后厨，途经上千个卧室、浴室、台球室和舞厅。酒流如水，时间总在朦胧中逝去。来到这里的人很少离开，而离开的人也很少缺席太久。他们以兰利厅为家，或者至少，兰利厅为他们提供了一个家。

Marble statues of devils line the aisles. They have wreaths over their horns, their lips are daubed scarlet as sin, their eyes are the colours of ash and sunlight. The detail is breathtaking: their lyres and lutes, flutes and fiddles, drums and dulcimers are so perfectly carved that, but for the material, they could be real.\r\n\r\nFrescoes depict a troupe of musicians marching towards a slender mirror: pipers, flautists, drummers, all. Everyone's heard of the daft actors who're attempting to stage the siege of New Winchester in a shed.\r\n\r\nThe historical production has run into difficulties. The director has been caught by the fever for hours, and spends his days on the Mountain. The lead actor has run off with a successful prospector. The producer is doing his best, but assistance is urgently required if the film's to succeed.\r\n\r\nThe Pernickety Factor expresses her displeasure at being involved in the cinema and returns to your locomotive for a smoke and the Gazette crossword.=卢米埃尔夫人的电影并不难找。每个人都听说过那些愚蠢的演员，他们试图在一个棚子里上演围攻新温彻斯特的故事。历史性的制作遇到了困难。导演已经发了好几个小时的烧，每天都在山上度过。主演与一个成功的探矿者私奔了。制片人正在尽力而为，但如果电影要成功，迫切需要援助。Pernickety Factor对参与电影制作表示不满，并回到你的机车上抽烟和看《公报》填字游戏。
Mme. Lumire, for all her many talents, has a shaky grasp of plot and a shakier grasp of history. You work with what you have, and dramatise the rise of the Tacketies; the back-room deals in the Round Table, the clandestine intrigues of Sweet Jane rather than the fall of New Winchester itself. Someone says afterwards the film felt more like a play than a film, as though that's a bad thing.=卢米埃尔夫人，尽管她有很多才能，但对情节的把握不稳定，对历史的把握更不稳定。你用你所拥有的东西工作，戏剧化地表现Tacketies的崛起；圆桌会议的幕后交易，Sweet Jane的秘密阴谋，而不是新温彻斯特本身的衰落。事后有人说，这部电影感觉更像一部戏剧，而不是一部电影，仿佛这是一件坏事。

Mme. Lumière has reopened a theatre beneath the arches of the Bishopbridge. Prominent Tacketies sit with London sympathisers. They have formed a brief truce, united in their loathing of the cramped velvet seats. A light flares on the plaster wall. The film begins. \r\n\r\nThe film is titled the 'Concupiscence of the Verdance'.  Flickering images on painted lenses jerk across the wall. The camera luxuriates in the collapsing brown flesh of a fruiting fungus, the flight of a sporing body, the sudden bursting of a violet fungal sac, the prolonged death spasms of a camera-man. There are gasps from the audience.=卢米埃尔夫人已在主教桥的桥拱下重开了一家剧院。钉鞋党的名人与亲伦敦派齐聚一堂。他们暂时休战，在对那局促的天鹅绒座椅的厌恶上达成一致。一道光芒在石膏墙上燃起。电影开始了。\n\n电影的标题是《青翠之欲》。彩色镜片上闪烁的影像在墙上跳动。镜头陶醉于倒下的结实真菌棕色的菌肉、一具被扔向空中长满孢子的尸体、一枚突然爆裂的紫色真菌囊，以及一位摄影师死前漫长而扭曲的痉挛。观众们倒吸凉气。

For tonight, and every night thereafter, is the Half-Light Masque.=一扇被遮光处理的舞厅窗户被打开，显露出一条通往黄昏时分（抑或是黎明时分）客厅的通道。[qvd:134291(Otherloom)]\n\n[qvd:134291(Governesses)]\n\n你穿过女皇的画像进入客厅，脚步蹒跚，因为刚才在黑暗中跳舞和跌跌撞撞，脚已经很疼了。你身后，是琥珀宫的成员们，他们闲聊着，品着茶，准备开始新的一天。因为从今晚起，之后的每个夜晚，都是明暗假面舞会。

One of the devils is a lapidarist, and begins cutting the gems into exact shapes.=其中一个魔鬼是个青石匠，开始把宝石切割成精确的形状。
One of the devils is a lapidarist, and begins cutting the gems into exact shapes. He carefully positions a candle in their midst, its light reflecting in brilliant beams from one jewel to another. You watch as, gem by gem, the heart of the engine is constructed from arcs of varicoloured light.\r\n\r\nOnce complete, it is a beating luminosity. It courses with colour, and dazzles the eyes. A devil encases the heart in a lead box, and installs it in the centre of the new engine.=其中一个魔鬼是宝石切割师，他开始将宝石切割成精确的形状。他小心翼翼地在宝石中间放置了一支蜡烛，烛光在宝石之间反射，闪耀着绚丽的光芒。你注视着，只见一颗颗宝石被用来构建机械之心，它由一道道色彩斑斓的光弧组成。\n\n一旦完成，它就成为了一个闪耀着光芒的心脏。它流淌着色彩，令人眼花缭乱。一个魔鬼将这个心脏装入一个铅盒中，并将其安装在新引擎的中央。

One of the factory's watchmen catches you in the act of lighting a fuse, and chases you away from the munitions. A hue-and-cry is raised. Several of your accomplices are arrested.\r\n\r\nHowever, in the wake of your attempt the factory increases security, inconveniencing the workers and draining much-needed resources. Progress slows.=工厂的一位看守在你点燃导火索时抓住了你，并将你从军火库里赶走了。他高呼警报。你的几个同伙被逮住了。\n\n然而，你的谋划使得工厂加强了安保措施，给工人们带来不便，还消耗了急需的物资。进度延缓了。

One prospector tells of finding a geode in the shape of a lion  apparently a mark of great fortune. Another talks of chipping away in silence so as not to startle the hours inside. Another mentions how cold the geodes are. As difficult as it is to work, a layer of thick ice underneath the snow is considered a sign of a good claim.\r\n\r\nThey all agree that the mining day must begin with a libation; a cup of moonshine poured to the mountain's good graces. If it rumbles, it is said the offering is accepted. If purple wisps appear over their claim afterwards, its prospector is blessed indeed.=一位探矿者说他发现了一块狮子形状的晶石，这显然是巨大财富的标志。另一个人说，为了不惊动里面的人，他一直在默默地凿开。另一位则提到，这些阳极石是多么的冰冷。尽管工作很困难，但雪下有一层厚厚的冰被认为是一个好矿区的标志。他们都同意，采矿日必须以酒开始；一杯月光酒倒给山的恩惠。如果它发出隆隆声，据说祭品就会被接受。如果事后在他们的矿区上空出现紫色的雾气，那么探矿者就真的受到了祝福。

Paimon is gone.=拜蒙已经走了。
Paimon watches as penitents quietly request their punishments.=帕蒙看着忏悔者安静地请求他们的惩罚。
Paimon watches as penitents quietly request their punishments. He observes the devils recommend exact castigations. Then, rapt, he stares as the penitents endure their punishment without complaint or immodest anguish. \r\n\r\nHe does not purr. Purring is not Paimon's way. But he admires the penitents' stoicism, and how Carillon administers sober, undramatic chastisement. Also, the devils steadfastly ignore him, which he seems to like. \r\n\r\nWhen you turn back for your locomotive, Paimon makes no move to follow.=拜蒙注视着忏悔者们冷静地请求惩戒。他看着魔鬼们为他们开出的严格惩罚。然后，他目不转睛地盯着忏悔者们忍受惩罚，他们一声不吭，也没有面露痛苦。\n\n他不发出咕噜声。拜蒙向来不屑于此。但他欣赏着忏悔者的坚忍，以及钟琴区的魔鬼们施行惩罚时冷静而又克制的样子。而且，魔鬼们完全忽略了他，这似乎让他很满意。\n\n你转头返回机车时，拜蒙没有跟上的打算。

Ratbite has made herself useful aboard your engine in the manner of all skylarks: part-passenger, part-dogsbody, working odd jobs around the locomotive to pay for her passage. When you track her down, she is busy helping the stokers at the engine.\r\n\r\nWhen you invite her to your cabin, she looks disappointed. Perhaps she suspects you're going to tell her to leave at the next port. Reports of a devastating battle above Titania are being reported. Several senior members of the Assembly have resigned, while the Windward Company is demanding the resignation of the Rhapsodic Mayor. The Gazette believes a planned raid by the Windward Company on a den of Tackety smugglers was almost thrown off course by the sudden intervention of a swarm of Chorister Bees. Most of the Company engines have been seen returning to Port Prosper. The Tacketies have vanished, or else perished altogether. =据报道，泰坦尼亚上空发生了一场毁灭性的战斗。议会的几个高级成员已经辞职，而Windward公司则要求狂想曲市长辞职。公报认为，向风公司计划对Tackety走私者的窝点进行突袭，但由于一群Chorister蜜蜂的突然介入，几乎被打乱了方向。人们看到公司的大部分发动机已经返回普罗斯珀港。Tacketies已经消失了，或者是完全消亡了。
Representatives of Pan's many factions crowd the stone seats.=潘氏众多派系的代表挤在石椅上。
Representatives of Pan's many factions crowd the stone seats. The revolutionaries of Winter's Reside, each wearing a flash of red. The placid gardeners of the Heart-Catchers. A crowd of flamboyant Neonocturnals. And a dozen other minor cults and coteries, colourful in Eleutheria's velvet darkness.\r\n\r\nEven a representative of the Brazen Brigade is here, a look of profound distaste on his elegant face. The Brigade dislikes anything that smacks of republicanism, in the same way that someone who once experienced bad prawns has no desire to do so again.=潘城众派系的代表聚集在石座位上。穿着一袭闪亮红衣的冬日之居革命者们。平静的捕心者园丁们。一群张扬的新夜行派。还有十几个其他的小教派和小团体，在厄琉忒里亚的天鹅绒黑暗中色彩斑斓。\n\n就连黄铜大队的代表也在这里，他优雅的脸上带着深深的厌恶。大队不喜欢任何带有共和主义味道的事物，就如同一个人一旦尝过难吃的虾就不想再尝一次一样。

The Displeased=不悦离人
The Displeased are indifferent to your existence.=不高兴的人对你的存在漠不关心。
The Displeased breed contempt from their familiarity with your person.=不高兴的人因熟悉你的人而滋生了蔑视。
The Displeased do not bother to say farewell. They have no expectation of your return.=不高兴的人懒得说再见。他们不期望你回来。
The Displeased have discovered you. They do not like you.=不高兴的人已经发现了你。他们不喜欢你。

The Grand Tournament stretches over countless acres of mud and filth. The air is filled with sobbing, incoherent shouting, screams; occasionally, the rhythmic thud of fists hitting flesh.\n\nThere are hundreds of questers wandering back and forth in the desolation, some more lucid than others. The Grand Tournament stretches over countless acres of the Queen's gardens. The air is filled with song, laughter, the roaring of crowds; occasionally, the clash and clang of weaponry. The Hermit accepts your offering and gestures for you to join them; to soothe the dying animal's pain in its last moments. They sift their fingers through its insides, plucking out organs and placing them on the ground in a careful but indecipherable pattern. When it is complete, the Hermit rests a compassionate hand on the beast's head and slits its throat in a smooth, practised manner. What they hoped to learn from this goes unspoken, but as you stand to leave, you see the pattern. An eye.=隐士接受了你的供品，并示意你加入他们；在最后时刻抚慰垂死动物的痛苦。他们用手指筛查它的内脏，拔出器官，并把它们放在地上，形成一个小心翼翼但难以辨认的图案。当它完成后，隐士将一只慈悲的手放在野兽的头上，以一种平稳、熟练的方式割断它的喉咙。他们希望从这里学到什么没有说出来，但当你站起来准备离开时，你看到了这个图案。一只眼睛。
The Hermit cups their hands beneath a gentle trickle of foul smelling water. They drink, then their words flow freely. They speak of the great charnel houses of Europe. How the Eagle will fight the Bear. How the Clockwork God will fall. A whisper of your own future too, never intended for your ears. A warning of what you may become in the dark.=隐士把他们的手放在散发着恶臭的水的温柔涓流下面。他们喝了水，然后他们的话语自由地流淌。他们谈到了欧洲的大墓室。鹰将如何与熊战斗。发条神将如何堕落。这也是你自己未来的低语，从未打算让你听到。一个关于你在黑暗中可能成为什么的警告。
The Hermit cuts a purple flower from their shoulder, licking the blood from the stem. They wrap it tight and place it in an old chipped cup full of gathered rainwater, stirring with the obsidian shard until it runs dark. They offer it. There is no refusing. When you wake up, only blessed fragments of nightmare remain. Burning at their core is an eye; the same one you now see repeated again and again in the Hermit's garden of flesh.=隐士从他们的肩膀上切下一朵紫色的花，舔着茎上的血。他们把它包得严严实实，放在一个旧的碎玻璃杯里，里面装满了收集的雨水，用黑曜石碎片搅拌，直到它流下黑水。他们提供它。没有人拒绝。当你醒来时，只剩下受祝福的噩梦碎片。在它们的核心燃烧的是一只眼睛；也就是你现在看到的在隐士的肉体花园里一次又一次重复的那只眼睛。
The Hermit drags a sharp rock through their flesh, carving spiral patterns on already bloodied skin. Their milky-grey eyes stare at something beyond the cave wall. Their whispers could as easily be prophecy or madness.=隐士将一块锋利的石头拖过他们的肉，在已经沾满血迹的皮肤上刻下螺旋状的图案。他们乳灰色的眼睛盯着洞壁之外的东西。他们的低语很可能是预言或疯狂。
The Hermit finishes carving their latest spiral and takes a drink from a gentle trickle of water running down from the roof of the cave. Their milky-grey eyes stare past you; their mouth occasionally forms a coherent word. Sweat builds on their brow. Their words might be truth, falsehood, or any flavour of madness in between.=隐士 完成了他们最新的螺旋形雕刻，从洞顶流下的涓涓细流中喝了一口水。他们乳灰色的眼睛盯着你过去；他们的嘴偶尔形成一个连贯的词。汗水在他们的额头上积聚。他们的话可能是真理，也可能是假话，或者是介于两者之间的任何疯狂的味道。
The Hermit lingers at the edge of sight, their rags the remnants of a zee-captain's uniform. Two of their eyes are closed tight. The third, carved with scars into their arm, seems to stare through you.=隐士们在视线的边缘徘徊，他们的衣衫褴褛，是一个Ze-captain的制服的残余。他们中的两个人紧闭着眼睛。第三只，在他们的手臂上刻着伤痕，似乎在凝视着你。
The Hermit sits motionless, meditating under a steady drip of water that feeds their garden of flesh. Their unblinking eyes pay you no attention as you take the candle deeper into the cave. Roses bloom in the dark, curling up and dying in the presence of the light.=隐士一动不动地坐着，在养活他们的肉体花园的稳定水滴下沉思。当你拿着蜡烛深入洞中时，他们一眨不眨的眼睛没有注意到你。玫瑰花在黑暗中绽放，在光线的照射下蜷缩起来并死去。

The Hermit takes your supplies, beckoning you into their cave. They shrink from the dim light of your candle, cowering and chewing on their ragged, bleeding fingernails. The cave rock shows the effort of their labours; wet crimson symbols and scratched down snippets from the other side of sanity. Behind them all, a truth to be whispered, but never spoken.=隐居者拿走你的补给，招呼你走进他们的山洞。隐居者们在你昏暗的蜡烛光线下缩成一团，蜷缩着，咀嚼着破溃流血的指甲。洞穴里的岩石展现了他们劳动的成果；潮湿的鲜红色的印记，还有从理智的另一面剥落的零星片段。在他们所有人的背后，是呼之欲出的真相，但从未被诉诸于口。
The Hermit whispers to the darkness. They pay you no mind as you look at their few remaining possessions. A trading log from a place far away, a faded photo of a love last seen in Old London. The Hermit's puckered skin is a mass of fungal blooms and the purple-leafed flowers of twilight. They tend to them with a sliver of obsidian, delicately carving weeds from their flesh.=隐士的褶皱皮肤是一团真菌的花朵和暮色中的紫叶花。他们用一截黑曜石照料它们，从它们的肉体上精巧地雕刻出杂草。

The Lyceum=学会
The Lyceum is a cavernous and crumbling vault.=学会是一个巨大空洞的、破碎的墓穴。
The Lyceum is a cavernous and crumbling vault. Its stone floors are covered in battered tomes and broken tablets. Creaking shelves far above you bow under the weight of disordered scrolls. \r\n\r\nA few thin rays of light filter in from holes in the towers high above. They illuminate vast stone stairs leading deeper into the Lyceum.\r\n\r\nThe Unworthy Scribe sits at a small desk beside the gate, whispering to himself and paying no heed to you.=学会是一个巨大的、摇摇欲坠的地窖。它的石头地板上布满了破损的书本和破碎的石板。高处的架子吱吱作响，上面堆满了杂乱的卷轴，不堪重负。\n\n几道细细的光线从高处的塔楼洞口透进来，照亮了通往学会深处的巨大石阶。\n\n微不足道的书记员坐在门边的小书桌前，自言自语，根本没有注意到你。
The Lyceum is a trove of buried knowledge; the lore of kings and regents; the notes on the creation of servants of the stars.=学会是一个埋藏知识的宝库；国王和摄政者的传说、星星的仆人们所创造的笔记。
The Lyceum is a trove of buried knowledge; the lore of kings and regents; the notes on the creation of servants of the stars. The scribes and clerks in the service of the Lamentation of Mists do what they can to organise and catalogue the vast archives, but the Lamentation's work comes first. The sky around is lit with cooling sparks from the Forge itself, its smouldered chimneys protected by the storeyed towers of the Lyceum. Here, knowledge is created.=学会是一个埋藏知识的宝库：国王和摄政者的传说、有关创造星星的仆人们的笔记。为迷雾哀歌服务的书记官和文书员们尽其所能地整理和编排庞大的档案，但哀歌的工作永远是第一位的。周围的天空被来自铸炉本身的冷却火花照亮，铸炉缓慢燃烧的烟囱被学会的层层塔楼保护着。在这里，知识被创造出来。
The Lyceum, the grand archive of the kingdom of the dead. And within it, the Forge of Souls, where the Stars once wrought new creations.=学会，死者之国的宏伟档案馆。灵魂铸炉正位于其中，群星曾在铸炉创造新的造物。

The Reserve is silent, at peace. The Ornithologist watches one horizon; you, the other. And then, you see it. It is no phoenix, burning through the sky. It is not an eagle, soaring. It is something else. Its feathers bear the weight of aeons and its glimmering beak, though dented and worn, holds a strength beyond any hammer-blow. This is the bird that will one day reduce the Mountain itself to dust. Eternity, close enough to reach out and touch.\r\n\r\nThe clattering of wood breaks the silence. The cat dives into your box of supplies, mewing joyously. When it's eaten its fill, it leaps free and trots off into the undergrowth.\r\n\r\nBefore it vanishes from sight, it pauses and gives you a meaningful look, then returns to your side. When it trots off a second time, you follow.\r\n\r\nThe stray leads you to a pair of ruinous, ivy-choked towers. The door to the first is blocked by rubble; the door to the second hangs from its hinges. The cat enters the latter. You follow. It leaps from stone to crumbling stone, higher and higher, occasionally pausing for you to catch up.=那只猫欢快地喵喵叫着，一头扎进了你的补给箱里。吃饱喝足后，它一跃而出，蹦蹦跳跳地跑进了灌木丛中。\n\n在它消失之前，停了下来，给了你一个意味深长的眼神，然后又回到了你身边。当它再次蹦蹦跳跳地离开时，你跟了上去。\n\n这只流浪猫带你来到两座破败不堪、爬满常春藤的塔楼前。第一座塔楼的门被碎石堵住了；第二座塔楼的门则摇摇欲坠地挂在铰链上。猫走进了后者，你也跟了进去。它在石块间跳来跳去，越跳越高，偶尔也会停下来等你跟上。

The cat sleeps in the hold. In the engine room. In the galley. It is often found asleep, never seen expending energy moving from one place of repose to another. Today, it is sleeping on your desk.=这只猫睡在车舱里，在引擎室里，在厨房里。它经常睡觉，从未有人见过它耗费精力从一个休息的地方移动到另一个休息的地方。今天，它就睡在你的桌子上。

The chambers of the Dreadnought have become an extended death trap. Slivers of glass fall from ceilings. Vitrified walls shatter as you pass, exposing you to the sky and its wind-blown shards. The chaperones are not used to visitors taking an interest in them; they are usually passed over in favour of their more elegantly appointed cousins. The chaperones are not used to visitors taking an interest in them; they are usually passed over in favour of their more elegantly appointed cousins. And indeed many of them are literal cousins, either impoverished or somehow reduced in society's eyes due to scandal or unfortunate connections. \r\n\r\nAll are past the age of marriage, and – at least as far as Society is concerned – the age of temptation, and are therefore fit companions to ensure the debutantes' dubious chastity. By the end of your conversation, their expressions have relaxed from 'pinched' to merely 'sour'.=监护人们向来不习惯访客对她们产生兴趣；比起这些寒酸亲戚，人们通常更青睐那些打扮光鲜的表亲姐妹。事实上她们中许多人确系名门之后，或因家道中落，或因丑闻牵连，终在世人眼中折了身份。\n\n她们皆已过了适婚年龄——至少在上流社会看来——也过了诱人的年华，故而成为确保闺秀们那可疑贞洁的合适监护者。谈话结束时，她们的神情已从“紧绷”缓和至“只是板着脸”。

The chaperones are restrained and even-tempered. Their compliments are not effusive, but they are sincere. The complete Song of the Sky meets with universal acclaim, hailed as the greatest modern iteration of the epic. You will never want for speaking engagements again, and your greatest hardship will be the constant demand for a sequel.\r\n\r\nFor years to come, scholars will pore over the Song, teasing apart the intricacies of its prose. They will debate its accuracy, its message, but not its merits (its merits are without question). Most of all, they will debate its ending  the captain's graceful retirement, described in such simple last lines. Why retire and return home after such a long and illustrious career? Was it a happy ending? Melancholy? Bittersweet? \r\n\r\nOnly the author knows.\r\n\r\nYour Song is sung; your story over; your name written across the skies.=完整的《天空之歌》受到普遍赞誉，被誉为最伟大的现代史诗迭代。你将不再需要演讲，而你最大的困难将是对续集的不断要求。多年来，学者们将仔细研究《天空之歌》，探究其散文的复杂性。他们会争论它的准确性，它的信息，但不是它的优点（它的优点是毫无疑问的）。最重要的是，他们会争论它的结局，即车长的优雅退休，在如此简单的最后几行中描述。为什么在经历了如此漫长和辉煌的职业生涯后要退休回家？这是一个幸福的结局吗？忧郁的？苦乐参半？\\只有作者知道。你的歌已经唱完了；你的故事结束了；你的名字写在天空中。

The contents of the allotments are unlike familiar vegetables, but it helps to look for the similarities. That bulbous squash is too lumpen, too spotty, too purple to be a marrow; but it is more like a marrow than it is like a cucumber. The little fruits clumped on the serpentine vines are certainly not cherries. Cherries are not hairy. But they are closer to cherries than they are to, say, kiwi fruit. Or otters.\r\n\r\nCall it a marrow, then. Call them cherries. It helps, somehow. The gardener, mistaking your cognitive reshuffle for hunger, offers you a handful of freshly-dug, tapered, tiger-striped roots. Let's call them carrots.=这些菜园里的作物并不像我们熟悉的蔬菜，但试着寻找相似之处会有帮助。那只鼓胀的南瓜过于笨重、斑点太多、颜色太紫，显然不是一种西葫芦；但它至少更像西葫芦，而不是黄瓜。缠绕在蛇形藤蔓上的那一小簇果实肯定不是樱桃——樱桃不会长毛。不过，它们与其说像奇异果或水獭，倒不如说更接近樱桃。\n\n那就叫它西葫芦吧。就把那些果实叫作樱桃。这样称呼，不知为何让人心里更好受些。园丁误把你这番认知上的重新整理当成了饥饿的信号，递给你一把刚从土里挖出来的，带着虎纹条纹的锥形根茎。我们就把它们叫作胡萝卜吧。

The Lords sit dead at their benches, surrounded by the empty bottles with which they happily drank themselves into oblivion. Your teeth feel like they have been welded together, your senses desert you for a moment.\r\n\r\nThen the lightning loses interest, and expends its wrath on a passing disgruntlement of cantankeri. You make your escape.=那闪电虽狂乱失措，其速度却仍然不下于你。它紧追着你的尾迹，向你的机车刺出锯齿状的火弧。电流顺着你的车身疾驰而过。你的牙齿仿佛被上下焊死，你的官能有一瞬间弃你而去。\n\n而后闪电失去了兴致，转而将它的怒火倾泻在一只路过的、愤愤不满的顽固虱身上。你逃了出来。

The net bulges, its cords straining against its contents. When cut, the strings fly back, flicking against the glass of your helmet. The contents spew forth. This is a short rod, with a bristle of brass spines at one end. Is it a key? A plaque of adamant, stamped with a blazing sigil. It is too bright to consider directly, and melts several mirrors when you try to examine it more obliquely. Is it a passphrase? A beacon? And finally, a doorknob, as found in a typical middle-class London home. =网子鼓起来了，它的绳索对它的内容物产生了压力。当被切断时，绳索飞回，弹到你头盔的玻璃上。里面的东西就会喷出来。这是一根短棒，一端有黄铜刺的鬃毛。这是一把钥匙吗？一个金刚牌，上面印着一个炽热的符号。它太亮了，无法直接考虑，当你试图更斜地检查它时，会融化几面镜子。它是一个口令吗？一座灯塔？最后是一个门把手，在一个典型的伦敦中产阶级家庭中发现。

The palace falls away.=宫殿倒下了。
The palace falls away. Your new shape twists, folds, retreats. The flaming symbols that have replaced your flesh extinguish one by one. The stones in your eye-sockets shatter into teardrops and crumble down your cheeks. \r\n\r\nIt is excruciating in a dozen different ways. The ache of a still-healing wound, the agony of scourged flesh, the pain of a bitter and dreaded departure. \r\n\r\nWhen it is finally over, you find yourself once more confined to the twitching, decaying flesh-wreck that is your body. You haven't outwardly changed, but every movement now feels lumpen and ponderous. The Carefree Attendant helps you to your feet with a smile.=宫殿崩塌。你的新形体不断扭曲、折叠、分解。取代你肉体的火焰符印一个接一个地熄灭。你眼窝里的石头碎成了泪珠，从脸颊上滑落。\\n\\n这个过程包含着十几种不同的痛苦，包括尚未痊愈的伤口的疼痛、肉体被鞭笞的痛苦、痛苦和恐惧的离别的痛苦。\\n\\n当改变最终结束时，你发现自己再次被困在一个不断抽搐的、会腐烂的、状况不佳的肉体中——这是你的身体。你外表没什么变化，但一举一动都显得笨重。无忧的侍从帮助你站起来。

The ritual comes easily to you. It begins with a cup of mere hot water, sipped to clear the taste-buds. Midnight Connoisseurs bring forth a bowl of embers on which to heat the ceremonial bronze kettle. You wait, eyes averted from the kettle so that it may boil, while your host prepares the implements. The sounds of the gramophone are louder here. Battered metal and tormented wood-panelling comprise the confines in which the crew dwelled. Chubby toadstools, round as pastries, dot the cramped bunkbeds. \r\n\r\nMementos of home are scattered about the fruiting debris. The wind bites.=风在咬人。
The wind bites. The gravel crunches underfoot as you approach the house. You are at the doorstep, now. Within is a vacant, desolate hallway, scattered with skeletal leaves.\r\n\r\nSuddenly, the wind picks up, slamming the door in your face. It grows in strength, howling at you, forcing you back to your engine. The gale tears away some of your belongings, dragging them into the sky. As soon as your boot is on the footplate, the mists fold in. Your engine jolts, suddenly adrift. The house is gone.=寒风凛冽。当你走近房子时，脚下的碎石发出嘎吱嘎吱的声响。此刻，你已来到门口。门内是一条空旷荒芜的走廊，散落着干枯的叶子。\n\n突然，风势增强，猛地一下把门摔在你脸上。风力愈发猛烈，呼啸着向你袭来，迫使你退回到机车旁。狂风卷走了你的一些物品，将它们拖向天空。你的靴子刚踏上踏板，浓雾便迅速笼罩四周。你的机车猛地颤动，突然间仿佛失去了方向。那座房子已经消失不见了。

We publish here, with only minor edits, a letter from the Prudent Secretary. \\Following the recent period of turbulence, it has come to our attention that the Windward Company has been approaching the New Winchester situation incorrectly. We are not unsympathetic to the charges put against us: namely rigidity, inflexibility, conspiracy and espionage. We somewhat resent 'indiscriminate terror' however. It has been anything but. Nonetheless, it has become apparent we lack the public support to continue as we are without needlessly and injuriously imposing our program on the unwilling. As such, we have invited the Assembly to reconvene on New Winchester, with our full and fulsome support. I feel compelled to make clear that the Windward Company does not regard this as a defeat, but rather a new opportunity for peaceful cooperation and bipartisanship in the Reach.\\n=我们在此发表谨慎秘书的一封信，只做了少量编辑。\\在最近一段时间的动荡之后，我们注意到，向风公司对新温彻斯特的情况的处理是不正确的。我们对针对我们的指控并非没有同情心：即僵化、不灵活、阴谋和间谍活动。但是，我们对 不分青红皂白的恐怖 有些反感。这不是什么好事。然而，我们显然缺乏公众的支持，无法继续我们的工作，也无法将我们的计划无谓地、有害地强加给不愿意的人。因此，我们已经邀请大会在新的温彻斯特重新召开会议，并得到我们充分和有力的支持。我觉得有必要明确指出，向风公司不认为这是一次失败，而是在达成和平合作和两党合作的新机会。

Work is slow on the new Salon, located just off Valentine Square. The Stone-Faced Sculptor waves away any questions or criticisms, determined only that whatever it turns out to be, it will be the finest example of it in the Reach.=新沙龙的工作进展缓慢，位于瓦伦丁广场附近。石脸雕塑家对任何问题或批评一笑置之，他只下定决心，无论结果如何，它都将是河内最好的例子。
Work is slow.=工作很慢。
Work is slow. Your engineers fumble at bolts, stumble on the dark hull, slip and let a perfectly good section of plating go spinning into the night. Then, for no clear reason, their lamps go out.\r\n\r\nThe engineers scramble back to your engine, and refuse to return to their task.=工作进展缓慢。你的工程师在螺栓上摸索，在黑暗的车体上磕绊、滑倒，让一块非常好的装甲板打着旋坠入黑夜。然后，他们的灯莫名其妙地熄灭了。\n\n工程师们争先恐后地回到你的机车，拒绝继续他们的工作。
Work is underway on the Academy for the Bloody Arts. It is not what they want; but it might be what they need.=血腥艺术学院的工作正在进行中。这不是他们想要的；但可能是他们需要的。
Work is underway on the Apollo Fortress. May it offer the Titanians some protection.=阿波罗堡垒的工作正在进行中。愿它为泰坦尼亚人提供一些保护。
Work is underway on the Astral Amphitheatre. Epic poetry will no longer be confined to pages alone; they shall be spoken again.=星空露天剧场的工作正在进行中。史诗将不再仅仅局限于书页，它们将再次被说出来。
Work is underway on the Empyreal Ballroom. The Titanians shall soon be dancing under the stars.=Empyreal舞厅的工作正在进行中。泰坦尼亚人很快就会在星空下跳舞。
Work is underway on the Imperial Cathedral. The hymns they shall sing will ignite future choirs.=帝国大教堂的工程正在进行中。他们要唱的赞美诗将点燃未来的唱诗班。
Work is underway on the Library of Yore. The historians' art will find no finer home than Titania.=昔日图书馆的工程正在进行中。历史学家的艺术将找到比泰坦尼亚更美好的家园。
Work is underway on the Light Opera House. Nowhere else in the Wilderness will you find comedy so incisive or penetrating.=轻型歌剧院的工作正在进行中。在荒野的其他地方，你无法找到如此精辟或透彻的喜剧。
Work is underway on the Lustful Palace. Love poems will blossom in its courtyards.=情欲宫的工作正在进行中。爱情诗将在它的院子里绽放。
Work is underway on the Observatory. The astronomical arts shall be practised here.=天文台的工作正在进行中。天文艺术将在这里得到实践。
Work is underway on the Queen's Head. The Titanians will have a home for their songs at last.=皇后之首的工程正在进行中。泰坦尼亚人终于有了一个唱歌的家。
Work is underway on the Saturnine Theatre. Titania shall soon have a home fit for Tragedy.=土星剧院的工作正在进行中。泰坦尼亚很快就会有一个适合上演悲剧的家。
Work is underway!=正在建造中！
Work is, inevitably, behind schedule. A delivery of hours might get things back on track.=工作不可避免地落后于计划。一个小时的交付可能会让事情回到正轨。

Workers are unhappy with their lot.=工人们对自己的命运感到不满。
Workers burst through into the Bit Between from the workworld. Overseers run in both directions  some fleeing, some throwing themselves into the melee.=工人们从工作区冲进位面之间。监督员们向两个方向跑去，有些人在逃，有些人则投身于混战之中。
Workers in neat uniforms guide your locomotive to rest. Tourist engines rest alongside trading engines; crews trade gossip and delicacies. Signs in block capitals make abundantly clear that this is a place for pleasure.=穿着整洁制服的工人引导你的机车停泊。旅游机车与贸易机车停在一起；乘务员交换闲言碎语和美味佳肴。大写字母的标志非常清楚地表明，这里是娱乐场所。
Working beside them, you can see their hands shake, their lips tremble.=在他们身边工作，你可以看到他们的手在颤抖，嘴唇在颤抖。
Working beside them, you can see their hands shake, their lips tremble. They don't speak. In an adjacent compartment, someone is weeping.=在他们身边工作时，你发现他们手指颤抖，嘴唇翕动。他们不发一语。相邻的车厢里，有人在哭泣。
Working in silence is difficult and, frequently, dangerous.=在沉默中工作是困难的，而且经常是危险的。
Working in silence is difficult and, frequently, dangerous. Some of the crew tire of it. They remove the plugs from their ears, and the winds flock to them, whispering and wheedling. The hapless crew follow them out into the sky.=在寂静中工作十分困难，且危险重重。一部分列车员已经厌倦了。他们拿下耳塞，风便奔涌而去，在他们耳边小声地循循善诱。无助的列车员们跟随着风跳入天空。

Worlebury-juxta-Mare dazzles like a Faberg egg, lamp-lit, rich brass and Britain in baroque. In the distance, carnival music mixes with faint cheering. A queue twists and snarls along the dock. Visitors are not allowed to just stroll into the port. They must be <i>admitted<\u002Fi>.\r\n\r\nEvery fortnight, the Bureau of Entertainments holds a lottery to give out a number of pauper's passes which grant free admittance. The queue for these is long, but it's not the only way into the port.=沃尔伯里-朱克斯塔-马雷就像一个法贝格蛋一样耀眼，灯火通明，丰富的黄铜和英国的巴洛克风格。在远处，狂欢节的音乐与微弱的欢呼声混合在一起。码头上的队伍蜿蜒曲折，排起了长龙。游客不允许随便进入港口。每两周，娱乐局都会举行一次抽奖活动，发放一些穷人的通行证，让他们免费进入。排队的人很多，但这不是进入港口的唯一途径。
Worlebury-juxta-Mare dazzles like a Fabergé egg, lamp-lit, rich brass and Britain in baroque. In the distance, carnival music mixes with faint cheering. A queue twists and snarls along the dock. Visitors are not allowed to just stroll into the port. They must be <i>admitted<\u002Fi>.\r\n\r\nEvery fortnight, the Bureau of Entertainments holds a lottery to give out a number of pauper's passes which grant free admittance. The queue for these is long, but it's not the only way into the port.=滨海沃伯瑞就像一颗法贝热彩蛋一样耀眼，灯火通明，有着华丽的黄铜和英国巴洛克风格建筑。在远处，狂欢节的音乐与幽幽的欢呼声混杂在一起。码头上排着长长的队伍，蜿蜒曲折。游客不得随意漫步进入港口。他们必须<i>被接纳<\u002Fi>。\n\n每两周，娱乐局都会举办一次抽奖活动，给穷人发放一些通行证，让他们免费进入。排队等候的队伍很长，但这并不是进入港口的唯一途径。
Worlebury-juxta-Mare has become a corpse.=Worlebury-juxta-Mare已经成为一具尸体。
Worlebury-juxta-Mare has become a corpse. The run-down bones of its forgotten attractions swarm with bedraggled men and women, all armed with cleaning equipment. This is where the workers of Worlebury live and labour to create the gaudy frontage seen by tourists. The beach is now a decaying mess  visited only by the cultists who attend the chapel there. \r\n\r\nTo linger here, you'll need to work. But labour is poorly paid  take other workers' jobs too often, and they'll firmly encourage you to depart.=沃尔伯里-朱克斯塔-马雷已经成为一具尸体。被遗忘的景点的破旧的骨头上挤满了衣衫褴褛的男人和女人，他们都拿着清洁设备。这里是沃勒伯里的工人们生活和劳动的地方，他们创造了游客看到的华丽的门面。海滩现在是一个腐烂的烂摊子，只有参加那里的小教堂的邪教分子才会来这里。\\要在这里逗留，你需要工作。但劳动的报酬很低，经常抢别人的工作，他们会坚定地鼓励你离开。
Worlebury-juxta-Mare has become a corpse. The run-down bones of its forgotten attractions swarm with bedraggled men and women, all armed with cleaning equipment. This is where the workers of Worlebury live and labour to create the gaudy frontage seen by tourists. The beach is now a decaying mess – visited only by the cultists who attend the chapel there. \r\n\r\nTo linger here, you'll need to work. But labour is poorly paid – take other workers' jobs too often, and they'll firmly encourage you to depart.=滨海沃伯瑞已经是一具尸体了。它被人遗忘的景点徒留残骸，挤满了手持清洁工具，衣衫褴褛的男男女女。这里就是沃伯瑞的工人们生活和劳作的地方，他们曾在此创造出游客所见的那片浮华景象。如今的海滩已是一片衰败，只有那些前往小教堂参加仪式的信徒们才会踏足此处。\n\n若想在此逗留，你就得工作。然而这里的劳动报酬微薄——如果你频繁抢夺其他工人的活计，他们会坚决地“鼓励”你离开。

Fortunately, someone drags you to safety before you come to any further harm.\r\n\r\nPerhaps the other events will be play more to your strengths.=你冲入战场，双腿立刻被人从身下扫倒。战斗在你四周激烈进行，践踏的靴子将你踢来踢去。等你踉跄着站起来时，已是遍体鳞伤，脑子也晕头转向。\n\n就在这时，一个魁梧壮硕的探险者跌跌撞撞地穿过人群，经过时几乎心不在焉地朝你脑袋挥了一拳。幸好，在你受到更多伤害之前，有人把你拖到了安全地带。\n\n也许其他项目会更有利于你发挥长处。

You get into what you think must be the queue. It doesn't move.\r\n\r\nYou stand. Then you sit. Then you lie down. Nothing moves.\r\n\r\nThe spirit of a fungal colony occupies a space next to you. You press on, towards the engine room.=你独自深入。你的列车员在身后消失，融入一片橙金色的迷雾之中。上方，附着在金属上的孢子囊开始爆裂。孢子和粘稠液体如雨般落下，令地形更加险峻。\n\n你泛起一种奇特的感觉。你的手在发抖，仿佛在渴望触摸真菌，就像渴望着再喝一杯酒。你加快了脚步。\n\n身后响起尖叫。你转身，看到一名特别不专心的信号员也跟着你进入了瘴雾。她的双手陷进了剧毒的金色真菌中，很快全身也被吞没了。\n\n最后，你跃过了最后一个嘶嘶作响的菌卵，发现自己站在引擎室门前。
You go alone. Your crew disappear behind you, lost in a haze of orange and gold. Above, sacs of sporing fungus encrusted to the metalwork begin to erupt. Showers of spore and viscous liquids render the terrain still more hazardous. \r\n\r\nYou feel a peculiar sensation; your hands tingle, as though wishing to reach out, to touch the fungus, as though for one more drink. You increase your speed. \r\n\r\nThere is a cry behind you. You turn, to see one of your crew, a particularly distractible signaller, has entered the miasma after you. You go down yourself, held by a length of rope.=你自己也下去了，被一条绳子牵着。
You go down yourself, held by a length of rope. Your crew wait beyond the flower, grim-faced.\r\n\r\nThe stoker looks up, panicked. Your hand takes hers. You go for a walk.=你去散步吧。
You go for a walk.\r\n\r\nYou rub your hands, and stamp through puddles, and breathe deeply of the fume-heavy London air. Even now, you can't help but feel there was so much left out. You'll never cram it all into the Seventh Canto. Indeed, it would be disastrous to try. \r\n\r\nYou're in mourning  for the Song itself, and for the impossible, unattainable version of the Song that will haunt you until you die, and for the story upon which the Song is based and which too now approaches its end. You will retire. What can you do, upon completing your masterpiece, except retire?=你去散步。你搓着你的手，踩着水坑，深深地呼吸着伦敦的浓郁空气。即使是现在，你也不禁觉得有很多东西被遗漏了。你不可能把它全部塞进《第七章》。事实上，试图这样做将是灾难性的。\\你在为这首歌本身哀悼，为这首不可能的、无法实现的歌的版本哀悼，这首歌将困扰着你，直到你死去，也为这首歌所基于的故事哀悼，现在它也接近尾声了。你将退休。完成你的杰作后，除了退休，你还能做什么？

It's too late to undo the damage, unfortunately, but you make a mental note to avoid working under such stress.=你趴在桌子上，疯狂地工作，试图克服挥之不去的不安。但这并不奏效。到了晚上，你的文件被墨迹涂抹得乱七八糟，而你头痛欲裂。\n\n第二天一早，你发现你在错误的栏目中记下了错误的数字，还不小心签字丢弃了一些补给。不幸的是，现在要挽回损失已为时过晚，但你在心里记住了要避免顶着这种压力工作。

You order your crew to change course to steer from the Weft, but it is too late. With a sound like torn canvas, another day writes itself over this one. You watch as one of your crew, his own time now inseparably tangled with one of the dying days in the Weft, withers, dies, and rots in a second.=你命令你的列车员改变航线，从纬线上转向，但为时已晚。伴随着帆布撕裂般的声音，新的一天书写下自己盖过今时。你看着你的一位列车员，他本身的时间正与纬线中一个垂死的日子紧紧纠缠，衰老、死亡和腐烂只在一瞬。
You order your crew to pitch in, donning wet suits and gathering cloth about your mouths. The leader of the Tacketies is the second lieutenant ("Captain went down when we were hit off the white arches."), who guides you through the creaking engine. \r\n\r\nThe ramshackle locomotive is seeping with marsh water, and reeks of damp. Accounting for all the crew and salvaging supplies takes hours, but the lieutenant will not relent till this is done.\r\n\r\nAs night draws in, she goes in with you one last time. At the bottom of the engine all but sunk in the marsh, is a heavy box that takes two to carry out. "We can get passage from here. Couldn't lose this."=你命令你的列车员加入进来，穿上潜水服，用布捂住嘴。钉鞋党的首领是少尉（“车长在我们被撞出白色拱门的时候倒下了。”），他引导你穿过吱吱作响的机车。\\n\\n破烂不堪的火车头浸泡在湿地水中，散发出潮湿的臭气。清点所有的列车员和打捞的物资要耗费数小时，但少尉在完成这些工作之前都不会松懈。\\n\\n当夜幕降临，她最后一次和你一起走进去。在机车底部，有一个沉重的箱子，需要两个人抬出来，它几乎沉没在沼泽地里。“我们可以从这里过去。不能把这个丢了。”

You order your locomotive plunged into darkness.=你命令你的机车陷入黑暗之中。
You order your locomotive plunged into darkness. Every lamp is quenched and emptied of oil. The crew manage as best they can by starlight, but accidents inevitably happen. Tensions rise.\r\n\r\nAfter a day, you light an experimental lamp. It burns yellow. You relight the others.=你下令将机车浸入彻骨黑暗。每盏车灯皆被掐灭，燃油倾尽。列车员们尽力就着星光工作，但事故还是不可避免地发生了。压抑渐如浓雾弥漫。\n\n昼夜轮转后，你点起一盏试燃灯。黄焰燃起。于是你点亮其他灯光。

You outline your conversations with the Ambassador of Albion.\r\n\r\n"It doesn't matter how long she contrives to squat in the Toll-Tower," he says, when you've finished. "She has a Clear soul. It is a flaw that comes from having no regard for death. She will never be welcome in the Blue Kingdom, and she will never understand its meaning. It would be kindest to send her home."=你概述了你与阿尔比恩大使的谈话。\n\n“不管她是否企图在渡灵塔里待上更久的时间，”在你解决租约后，他说道，“她有一个澄明的灵魂。这是一个缺陷，源于为死亡的不敬。蓝色王国永远不会接纳她，她也永远不会理解这个国度的真谛。送她回家是最好的做法。”

You paddle through the shallows today, your head held up in the air. As it turns out, it was a good decision. The mists are unusually attractive, opalescent pink with a gilding of gold.=你今天划过浅滩，抬头挺胸。事实证明，这是一个好的决定。迷雾异常迷人，乳白色的粉红色，带着金色的镀层。
You paint the fascinated MPs a tale of the wonders and hardships outside of their parliamentary cocoon, taking care to sprinkle in a few embellishments when they seem to be on the verge of dozing off.=你向着迷的议员们讲述他们议会茧外的奇迹和艰辛，注意在他们似乎快要打瞌睡的时候撒上一些点缀。
You paint the fascinated MPs a tale of the wonders and hardships outside of their parliamentary cocoon, taking care to sprinkle in a few embellishments when they seem to be on the verge of dozing off. It may not all sink in, but they won't quickly forget the gory details.=你向感兴趣的议员们讲述议会茧房之外的各种奇迹和苦难故事，同时在他们快要打瞌睡的时候，细心地加上一些细节点缀。也许他们不能完全理解你的发言，但不会转头就忘记那些血淋淋的细节。

You pass near a sea of rolling mists. How languorous they are. How soft and how grey.=你经过一片翻滚的雾海。何等迟缓，何等柔和，何等灰黯。
You pass the man the egg; he almost drops it.=你把鸡蛋递给他；他几乎要把它扔掉。
You pass the man the egg; he almost drops it. He then searches around under the stall for a while  with the egg tucked dangerously under his arm.  Eventually, he gives up looking for a container to stow it in and clutches it between his legs while he roots through his pockets to pay you. Finally, with a nervous smile, he tips the right amount onto the counter in front of him.=你把鸡蛋递给那个人；他差点把它摔了。然后他在摊位下搜索了一阵子，鸡蛋被危险地夹在胳膊下。 最后，他放弃了寻找可以存放鸡蛋的容器，把鸡蛋夹在两腿之间，同时从口袋里掏出钱来给你。最后，他带着紧张的微笑，把适量的钱放到他面前的柜台上。
You pass the man the egg; he almost drops it. He then searches around under the stall for a while – with the egg tucked dangerously under his arm.  Eventually, he gives up looking for a container to stow it in and clutches it between his legs while he roots through his pockets to pay you. Finally, with a nervous smile, he tips the right amount onto the counter in front of him.=你把蛋递给他。他几乎没能拿稳。他在摊子下方摸索了一阵，在此过程中，蛋一直被他用一种危险的方式夹在在胳膊底下。然后，他终于放弃寻找合适的容器，转而把蛋夹在两腿之间，然后从口袋里搜出付给你的钱。最后，他面带紧张的笑容，按照说好的数目把钱币放在了面前的柜台上。
You pass through the Roosts, an archipelago of silent ruins.=你穿过栖息地，这是一片寂静的废墟群岛。
You pass through the fog of smoke and speculation, where opinionated old matrons discuss the inherent perfidy of devils, and the impossibility of true repentance in the human soul.=你穿过香烟和猜疑的迷雾，有主见的老妇人们在其中讨论魔鬼与生俱来的背信弃义，以及人类灵魂真正忏悔的不可能性。
You pass through the frenzied displays.=你通过了狂热的展示。
You pass through the frenzied displays. Your crew have torn their uniforms and daubed themselves with oil. The galley is smeared with filth. In the engine room, books burn in the fire-grate. \r\n\r\nThis crewman needs bandaging, after they rested their face against the boiler as if it was a pillow. This one needs to be restrained for the protection of others. This one only needs tea and a fungal biscuit. Gradually, the scales begin to tip. \r\n\r\nHave you weathered the wildness? Or have you only bought their sanity with your own?=你走过列车员们疯狂的惨相。他们撕裂自己的制服，用油抹遍全身。走廊上遍布秽物。引擎室里，书本正在火炉中燃烧。\n\n这个列车员把锅炉当成枕头，把脸放了上去，现在需要包扎。这个需要绑起来，以保护其他人。这个只需要一点茶和真菌饼干。终于，天平开始倾斜了。\n\n你经受住天野的考验了吗？还是说你付出自己的理智，才换来了他们的？

You pay the hour-vendors' disgraceful fee.=你付给钟点工可耻的费用。
You pay the hour-vendors' disgraceful fee. They deliver the hours to the relay's looms. Clanking and grinding, the looms spin the jacket of fresh time in which your locomotive will make its journey. \r\n\r\nEnclosed in your engine's pocket of hours, it is hard to say how long the passage will take. Unseasoned hours tend to be melancholy and anxious; your journey is likely to be wearing. \r\n\r\nThe machinery grinds and stirs. The steam vents. The sigils of the edifice burn with sullen fire. A force like a great hand seizes your engine.=你给时间贩子付了一笔巨款。他们把木桶送到中继站里发出叮当声和研磨声的时轮上。时轮正纺织着用以在航行时像外套一样包裹机车的新鲜时间。\\n\\n在机车的崭新时间外套的包裹下，很难说这段旅程需要多长时间。未加工的时间往往显得忧郁和焦虑，你的旅程可能会很颠簸。\\n\\n机械摩擦旋转。蒸汽喷薄而出。大楼上的符印燃着阴郁的火焰。一股宛如巨大手掌的力量攥住机车。
You perch precariously on the edge of the vast eye.=你岌岌可危地栖息在巨大的眼睛边缘。
You perch precariously on the edge of the vast eye. The Fluke quakes; its flesh ruptures, releasing spurts of caustic vapours. This close, your sky-suit cannot entirely protect you: when you finish coughing, the dizziness is overwhelming. You can smell the Fluke's dying wishes, are ravaged by its regrets: the search it leaves incomplete; its fear that the search is impossible and will never end; the jagged, excruciating recollections of being outcast and the certainty that only the outcast have a chance of success.\r\n\r\nEventually, an engineer works their way from your engine to help you back. Once you're through the external hatch, a stoker wordlessly passes you a cup of tea.=你摇摇欲坠地站在巨瞳边沿。锚虫颤抖着；它的肉体破裂，释出一股腐蚀性的气体。如此之近，以至你的潜天装并不能全然保护你；咳嗽之后，紧随而来的是压倒性的晕眩。你能闻见锚虫的遗愿，被它的遗憾所摧躏：它留下未竟的搜索，它害怕这搜索不可能完成，且永无结束之日：有关被弃的嶙峋而苦痛的回忆以及对仅有被弃者才有机会成功的确信无疑。\n\n最终，一位工程师将在你的机车内以他的方式助你把意识拉回。当你通过外部舱门，一个司炉无言地递给你一杯茶。

You place the tea leaf on your tongue. Fire. Cold fire. The predator. The stalker. The final drink at the end of a long night. The click of the lock. The control of stick and rope. The rush. The cold that follows. A hatred turned inwards. An escape into Midnight, where sins are absolved. The wolf muzzled, never to hunt again. The wolf leashed in the darkness, growling and awaiting its chance to break free.=你将一片茶叶放于舌上。火，冷冽的火。掠食者。追猎者。长夜将尽的最后一杯。锁具咔哒作响。绳与棍的支配。狂奔。紧追不舍的寒意。憎恶转头向内。一场没入午夜的逃亡，彼处罪恶得赦。狼被制住牙口，永远不可狩猎。狼被缚于黑暗，咆哮伺机欲脱。
You place the tea leaf on your tongue. The taste of ash, of words unsaid. The cold corpse in the bed, beyond recrimination or apology. The guilt of the abuser's silent partner, their crime being the choice to look away, again and again until ignorance was no longer a blanket. Every last word said in anger, and every naive conceit that regret owes anyone a second chance. The whisper of what could have been, curled up in the darkness of Midnight and drowned by its depths.=你将一片茶叶放于舌上。未曾出口的话语，那灰烬的滋味。卧榻之上的冰冷尸体，指责或道歉都不再与其有关。施暴者同伙的罪孽，便是选择视而不见，一而再，再而三，直到无知的遮羞布不再奏效。每一句愤怒的遗言，每一次自以为懊悔总能换来机会的幼稚妄想。来自本可成真之事的低声絮语，全都蜷缩于午夜的黑暗中，淹溺在它的深渊下。

You place your eggs on the counter  only for the man to knock one of them off with his elbow. He catches it as it falls, demonstrating luck, not coordination. He then searches around under the stall  with the egg tucked precariously under his arm. Eventually, he gives up looking for a container to stow it in and just places the eggs on the floor behind him. He will no doubt trip over one and shatter the lot.\r\n\r\nHe digs in his pockets, pulling out handfuls of coins and depositing them on the counter. When he has finished, he gives you a nervous smile. The transaction is, apparently, concluded.=你把鸡蛋放在柜台上，但那人却用肘部把其中一个鸡蛋打掉。他在鸡蛋掉下来的时候接住了它，这说明了他的运气，而不是协调。然后，他在摊位下四处寻找，鸡蛋不稳定地夹在他的胳膊下。最后，他放弃了寻找一个可以存放鸡蛋的容器，只是把鸡蛋放在他身后的地板上。他无疑会被一个鸡蛋绊倒，然后摔得粉碎。他在口袋里掏了掏，掏出几把硬币，放在柜台上。当他完成后，他给了你一个紧张的微笑。显然，这笔交易已经结束。

You place your hand on the idol; the moment your skin touches the burnished gold you find yourself somewhere else. Somewhere lightless and close. A wing, soft as a moth's, huge as a tapestry brushes your arm. She bids you tell her your secrets. \r\n\r\nWhen you are done, she tells you of a great war fought before the devils fell; of a new Conjunction in heaven; of diets of war and of peace; of counsels betrayed and feasts where the sky ran with spilt starlight; of the death of a king, and the end of all idylls in Eleutheria. She offers lamentations for the dead and the undeparted.\r\n\r\nHer innumerable voices are so thorough so precise in their gestalt descriptions that it is as if she was drawing a map on the fabric of your memory=你把手放在神像上。当你的皮肤接触到抛光的黄金时，你发现自己身处别处。某个无光而闭锁的地方。一只翅膀，柔软如蛾翅，广大如织锦，拂过你的手臂。她让你说出你的秘密。\\n\\n当你说完后，她告诉你魔鬼倒下之前发生的一场伟大的战争；天穹中的一个新生和相；战乱与和平时期的议会；被背叛的忠告和星光闪耀之处的盛宴；王之死，以及厄琉忒里亚内一切田园牧歌的结束。她为死者和未死者发出哀叹。\\n\\n她无数的声音是如此透彻，描述得如此精确，就像她在你的记忆的织布上画了一张地图。

Your train becomes just a patch of shadow, floating silently through the dark. \r\n\r\nPerhaps if you do nothing, there will be no point in the stars observing you any longer? Will you fade from view?\r\n\r\nYou settle cross-legged in your quarters, as the cold wind scourges your tomb-silent train. All is silent. All is still. You wait to find out.\r\n\r\n[Your captain has met their end.]=你在床位之间徘徊，收走眼睛。你的列车员们不会再盯着谁看了。\n\n要想躲避星星的注视则没那么简单。你停下引擎。你熄灭灯光。你抛掉所有的燃料和补给。你的火车成为一片影子，静静地在黑暗中漂浮。\n\n也许如果你什么都不做，星星就没必要再观察你了？你会从它们的视野中消失吗？\n\n你在舱室里盘腿坐下，寒风在你的坟墓——寂静的火车中肆虐。一切都安静了。一切都停止了。你等着答案出现。\n\n[你的车长走向了末路。]
You prowl from bed to bed, taking what you need.=你在床位之间徘徊，拿走你需要的东西。
You prowl from bed to bed, taking what you need. The stolen eyes slot neatly into your eager sockets. A few eager blinks causes a ripple of eyelids across your body.\r\n\r\nA wild laugh, pure bubbling joy, bursts from your lips as you open the hatch and feel the burning-cold wind on your face. Soon you shall meet the gaze of the stars, and gaze across eternity.\r\n\r\nYou step confidently into the sky.=你在床位之间徘徊，拿走你需要的东西。你偷来的眼睛被整齐地放进渴望的眼窝。几次热切的眨眼使你全身上下的眼皮泛起涟漪。\r\n\r\n你打开舱门，感受脸上灼热的冷风，嘴唇中迸发出一阵狂笑。这是纯粹而无法压抑的极乐。很快你就会对上星星的眼光，凝视整个永恒。\r\n\r\n你自信地踏向天空。

You pry away a great sheet of it as the hull buckles and sends a thousand knives of glistening glass razoring through your crew.=当车体弯曲，一千把闪闪发光的玻璃刀划过你的船员时，你撬开了一片巨大的玻璃刀。
You pry away a great sheet of it as the hull buckles and sends a thousand knives of glistening glass razoring through your crew. Blood mists the sky.=当其弯曲时，你撬开了一大片车体，并使无数闪闪发光的玻璃碎片从你的列车员身上划过。天空中血雾弥漫。
You pry the door open.=你撬开了门。
You pry the door open. Inside, is the throat of a short tunnel  connective tissue, really  leading out into a star-swallowed twilight.=你撬开了门。里面是一条短隧道结缔组织的咽喉，真的通向星空吞噬的黄昏。
You pry the door open. Inside, is the throat of a short tunnel – connective tissue, really – leading out into a star-swallowed twilight.=你撬开了门。里面是一个由真的结缔组织构成的短隧道的咽喉，通向被群星吞没的暮色。
You pry the lid off.=你把盖子撬开。
You pry the lid off. Dear God! What the blazes? Your navigator pokes the thing inside with a big stick, until assured that it's dead.=你撬开了盖子。亲爱的上帝! 这到底是什么？你的领航员用一根大棍子捅了捅里面的东西，直到确信它已经死了。
You pry the lid off. Dear God! What the blazes—? Your navigator pokes the thing inside with a big stick, until assured that it's dead.=你撬开了盖子。上帝啊！那究竟是什么？领航员用一根大棍子戳着里面的东西，最终确定它已经死了。
You publish in the Gazette.=你在《公报》上发表。
You publish in the Gazette. Will the Host please see his attendants are living up to their potential. A general lament for falling standards. A more specific plea that Magdalene's does not debase itself with cheap tricks like a parlour clairvoyant. You complain at length about the laughable fakeries of their 'general'.\r\n\r\nEveryone reads the Gazette. Magdalene's won't be offering the services of dead soldiers again anytime soon.=你在《公报》上发表文章。恳请主管关注他的侍者是否完全发挥了他们的潜力。这是一篇对服务水平下降的宽泛哀叹。一个更具体的恳求是，希望抹大拉之家不要像客厅灵媒那样用廉价的伎俩来贬低自己。你长篇累牍地抱怨他们“将军”那可笑的假动作。\\n\\n所有人都读《公报》。抹大拉之家很快就不会再提供死去士兵的服务了。
You pull a spare pillow over your head to mute the glassy tapping.=你把一个备用枕头拉到你的头上，使玻璃般的敲击声静音。
You pull a spare pillow over your head to mute the glassy tapping. Still you can hear it.\r\n\r\nTap-tap. Tap-TAP. TAP-TAP. Tap-TAP-tap-tap. TAP-TAP-TAP. TAP-tap. Tap. Tap-TAP-tap-tap. TAP-tap-TAP-TAP.=你把一个备用枕头拉到头上，来隔绝玻璃上的敲击声。但你还是能听到。\n\n轻-轻。轻-重。重-重。轻-重-轻-轻。重-重-重。重-轻。轻。轻-重-轻-轻。重-轻-重-重。
You pull at the knot with trembling hands.=你用颤抖的手拉开绳结。
You pull away the loose stone locking the nearest barrow. Your crew move away the other rocks, opening the graves. \r\n\r\nA cacophony of sound rolls out. Sigils smoulder in the air. 'NOT TO BE FORGOTTEN.' 'NOT TO SERVE.' 'NOT TO BE SILENT.' 'TO BE PERMITTED.' \r\n\r\nAsh and smoke blow across the now bellowing graves. One of the barrows is screaming in Latin. An erudite stoker conjugates in haste. "Captain," he shouts in your ear. "Those are your orders, from only yesterday. They've been listening."\r\n\r\nPeering inside the nearest barrow, you find it clogged entirely with stone, as though smothered. No wonder the voices sound so ragged, buried beneath mountains worth of rock.=你挪开堵住近处荒冢的石块。列车员们搬走其他石头，打开坟墓。\n\n嘈杂的声音从中涌出。冒烟的符印在空气中显现。“不要被遗忘。”“不要侍奉。”“不要沉默。”“要被允许。”\n\n灰烬和浓烟吹过咆哮着的坟墓。其中一座荒冢正用拉丁语尖叫。一个博学的司炉急忙拼写。“车长，”他在你耳边喊道。“这都是你昨天刚下的命令。它们一直在听着。”\n\n你向最近处那个荒冢内窥视，发现它被石头完全堵住，像被闷死了一样。难怪这些声音听起来如此粗粝，它们被埋在几座山那么多的岩石下面。

You pull out of the relay, and head back into the blanket of mists.=你离开了中继站，回到了茫茫的迷雾中。
You push back into the public house, to see every poet in the room hailing the Incognito Princess, trying to find couplets to exactly chart the bounds of her perfection. \r\n\r\n"Not so blue now, my sad rhymers!" she says, waving encouragingly at the poets, "You can find the words. If not English, perhaps words more celestial?" After a brief moment, they find a language whose shapes sound ill-fitted for a human palate. They rush on, joyously.\r\n\r\nOne poet's tongue ignites. Then another. Then a third. Soon, every poet has a mouthful of flame, and still they don't stop. In the middle of the conflagration stands the Princess, beaming.\r\n\r\nThis seems to be contagious. Best run.=你挤回酒店，看到房间里的每位诗人都对着隐姓埋名的公主欢呼，试图找到能准确描绘她完美境界的对句。\n\n她说：“现在不那么忧郁了，我的悲情韵者们！”她鼓励地朝诗人挥手，“你们可以找到那些词语。如果在英语里找不到，或许在更天体一点的语言里？”片刻之后，他们找到了一种语言，其音韵之优美，仿佛与人类的味蕾格格不入。他们欢快地四处奔走起来。\n\n一个诗人的舌头被点燃了。然后是另一个。然后是第三个。很快，每个诗人都有满嘴火焰，他们仍然没有停止。公主站在这场大火的中心，笑颜如花。\n\n这症状似乎会传染。该跑了。

You push but you only manage to distress your garments. The Princess' patience gives way and she whistles. Everyone in front of her falls to the ground; she walks over their bodies. You follow her to the front.\r\n\r\nYou look up at a poet staring into the middle distance, describing the misery of the hour-looms. Soon another poet steps on the stage, adding her own thoughts on how extraordinarily well the Princess compares to the first day of spring.  Then a third. You push on despite the howling wind and clashing thunder. Lightning scythes the sky. Your crew trudge on behind you, up hill and through valley, sliding on sodden ground, cowering from thunder roaring like dragons. \r\n\r\nEventually, the sky clear clears and you emerge into a dell. You push on. There is a brief scream behind you, and when you look back, she is gone. The golden fungus looks a little larger, and bulges unpleasantly. \r\n\r\nYou run on, towards the engine room, before the cloud of spores can do any further damage to you.=你继续前进。身后传来一声短促的尖叫，当你回头时，她已经不见了。金色的真菌看起来更大了一些，并且令人不快地鼓胀起来。\n\n在孢子云造成任何更多伤害之前，你继续向引擎室跑去。

You take the seal.=你爬下潮湿的岩壁，进入洞穴。几分钟后，你的眼睛才适应了光线。\n\n这个洞穴并非天然形成。墙壁上覆盖着青铜木，镶嵌有曩缚咤宝石——嵌得太深，无法取出。远处的星光从洞口反射到岩石上，使得洞穴充满了光芒。\n\n在洞穴的后方，你发现了一个王冠大小的银印章，与一把弯曲的月牙形刀刃。刀片的破碎金属上刻有信符。它太大了，无法移走，但你记录了这些符印。也许有位学者能够翻译出来。你取走了印章。

You will have to look to more desperate measures.=你搜遍每个柜子和小隔间，但找到的东西只能让发动机饥饿的火苗再撑几分钟。寒冷已在加剧。它会伤害你的列车员。你将不得不采取更孤注一掷的措施。

You searched the heavens and found no one. But you followed the trail Langley left behind. The shoes even fit.=你找遍了天际，却没有找到任何人。但你沿着兰利留下的足迹走了过去。鞋子甚至很合脚。
You secured your fame in academic circles with your masterpiece: a remarkable invention that pushed the boundaries of engineering. You can be of use.=你以杰作树立了在学术界的名声：一个推动了工程界的卓越发明。你可以让它派上用场。
You see not what is, but what should be. You remember not what was, but what should have been.=你所见的并非当下，而是理应如此的光景。你所忆的并非曾经，而是本应发生的过往。
You see nothing amiss.=你没有看到任何不妥。
You see nothing amiss. At least, there is nothing immediately amiss. The Lanes are tawdry but colourful, the shops lavish with pointless baubles. It is all quite normal. Yet still, something gnaws at your brain stem like a tapeworm that'd found its way up your spine, an insistence that maybe, maybe something is very, very wrong?=你看不出有什么不妥。至少，没有立即发现什么不对劲的地方。巷民很俗气，但色彩斑斓，商店有很多毫无意义的装饰品。这一切都很正常。然而，仍然有东西在你的脑干上咬着，就像一条在你的脊柱上找到的绦虫，坚持地认为也许，也许有什么东西非常，非常的不对劲？

You see the dividends our work has produced! I have students of my own! Stipends! Grants! Though - between you and me - the College has not sent its best. And not nearly enough funds to cover further exploration. But we are making progress. My Charlemagne will be woken soon enough. And you shall have the credit of helping me find him.=你看到我们的工作所产生的红利了吧！我有自己的学生了！。我也有自己的学生了! 津贴! 补助金! 虽然--在你和我之间--学院没有派出最好的。也没有足够的资金来支付进一步的探索。但我们正在取得进展。我的查理曼很快就会被唤醒。而你将拥有帮助我找到他的功劳。
You see the hazy shape of the Princess through the door.=你透过门看到了公主的朦胧身影。
You see the hazy shape of the Princess through the door. There's no time to waste. You take the candle and push it into your still-story-spouting mouth. The beeswax crunches between your teeth, the flame still burning as you gag down every part of the candle. Afterwards, you feel it burn brightly inside you.\r\n\r\nBut for the flame and pain, one thing does end. The story. You stopped telling the story as soon as you swallowed the candle. You hear the princess make an oddly strained cry of surprise tinged with despair. \r\n\r\nThe door is gone. The princess is trapped.\r\n\r\nIt's only then that you realise something hard and sharp is still in your hand. The Princess' tiara. Her finest. Yours now.=你透过门看到公主朦胧的身影。没有时间可以浪费了。你拿起蜡烛，把它推到你那还在向外喷吐故事的嘴里。蜂蜡在你的牙齿间嘎吱作响，当你把蜡烛全部塞进嘴里时，烛火仍在燃烧。之后，你便感觉到它在你体内熊熊燃烧。\n\n但在火焰和痛苦中，有一件事确实结束了。那个故事。当你吞下蜡烛时，你就不再讲故事了。你听到公主发出一声奇怪而紧张的，带着绝望的惊呼。\n\n门不见了。公主被困住了。\n\n直到这时，你才意识到有一个坚硬而锋利的东西还在你手中。公主的头饰。她身上最精致的物件。现在是你的了。

It has said too much.=你坐在一棵参天古树的根部，它的藤蔓在思考。只有你们两个人，Eleutheria的法律只允许将一个故事讲给另一个人。\\悬空的头颅在辩论你的问题。一个提供了一个假设，另一个提供了一个对立面。其余的人就综合问题进行协商。你记录下他们的发现。在你听的过程中，你了解到埃卢瑟亚的历史片段。在与Solonacean Conjunction的战争中取得了昂贵的胜利。半身人的悲痛。第二位讲故事的人的来访，捕心者陷入了沉默。它已经说得太多了。
You sit among the roots of a gnarled old Heart-Catcher as its vines coil in thought. It's just the two of you – the laws of Eleutheria only permit a tale to be told to one other person. \r\n\r\nThe hanging heads debate your question. One provides a hypothesis, another an antithesis. Where to begin?\r\n\r\nYou remember the look in the Publisher's vaguely reptilian eyes when you first told him this story  a mix of disbelief, awe, and half-concealed greed. The story stirs in your mind like some disturbed undersea monster, unspooling its tendrils, before rushing Leviathan-like to the surface.=你坐在你的书桌前。你站起来，你踱步，你又坐下。你凝视着窗外。你记得当你第一次告诉出版商这个故事时，他那隐约可见的爬行动物的眼神，混合着不相信、敬畏和半掩饰的贪婪。他是一个比空白页更亲切的听众。你开始打字，记得你在第一次讲故事时是如何措辞的。很快，打字机咔咔作响，欢快地响着。故事在你的脑海中搅动，就像一些不安的海底怪物，展开它的卷轴，然后像利维坦一样冲向水面。

You sit. You lose feeling in your legs. Sometimes, you see another Ape rise from its place. You take the helm.=你来掌舵。
You take the helm. It is a risky course. Sudden ruins loom out of the fog, requiring frantic changes of course. You wander lost for hours, until your legs cramp from walking up and down tens of thousands of stairs. Its back is to you, but its head is turned, one milky eye catching yours.\r\n\r\nYou examine the ruins. There is no child there. Only the tumbled stone, the moss, and the wind that whistles through the ruin. You leave quickly. The walk has not been as soothing as you hoped.=一阵刺耳的口哨声打断了你的宁静。一位画家正在这里，他一丝不苟地在高大的画布上用油画颜料重现废墟。他添加了一些内容：在一块突出的石头上，他画了一个衣衫褴褛的孩子坐在地上，膝盖蜷缩着。孩子的皮肤苍白如粉笔。他的背对着你，但头却转了过来，一只乳白色的眼睛与你的目光相遇。\\n\\n你仔细检查了废墟。那里并没有孩子。只有倒塌的石头、苔藓和穿过废墟呼啸而过的风。你迅速离开了。这次散步并没有像你希望的那样让人心旷神怡。
Your peace is interrupted by a whistling: a popular tune, appallingly executed. A painter is here. He has set his back to a towering arch, and is painting its reflection from a mirror set beside his easel. The mirror's glass is black, dulling the vibrant green of the moss and the scintillating hues of the sky. \r\n\r\n"The truly picturesque requires a certain restraint," he explains, frowning irritably over his shoulder at the splendid view. "This is trying rather too hard, don't you think?" His presence has ruined the atmosphere, but your walk is not unpleasant.=一阵刺耳的口哨声打断了你的宁静：那是一首流行歌曲，演奏得极其糟糕。一位画家在这里。他背对着高耸的拱门，正在画板上方的镜子里描绘拱门的倒影。镜子的玻璃是黑色的，使青苔的鲜绿色和天空的闪烁色调变得暗淡。\n\n“真正如画的美景需要一定的节制，”他解释道，同时烦躁地转过头去，皱着眉头看着壮丽的景色。“这太过分了，你不觉得吗？”他的出现破坏了气氛，但你的散步并不因此不快。
